description.narrative: The Project Development Objectives (PDOs) are to improve delivery of select health services, strengthen health management systems, and in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it.

The development objective of Health Systems Strengthening Project for Tuvalu are to improve delivery of select health services, strengthen health management systems, and in case of an eligible crisis or emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it. This project has four components. 1) The first component, Improve the Availability of Essential Public Health and Health Care Services Provided at Princess Margaret Hospital, has the following sub-components: (i) Increase the Physical Capacity of the Princess Margaret Hospital; and (ii) Increase the Human Resource Capacity of the Princess Margaret Hospital. 2) The second component, Strengthen the Delivery of Primary Health Care and Primary Prevention, with a Focus on Non-Communicable Diseases, has the following sub-components: (i) Improve the Delivery of Essential Primary Health Care Services at the Health Clinics, with a Focus on Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD) Services; and (ii) Strengthen Public Health Approaches to Primary Prevention and Behavior Chan. 3) The third component, Support the Development of Management Systems, has the following sub-components: (i) Strengthen Management Systems for Better Service Delivery; and (ii) Project Management, Monitoring and Technical Support. 4) The fourth component, Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC), aims to support a rapid response and urgent assistance in respect of an event that has caused, or is likely to imminently cause, a major adverse economic and/or social impact to Tuvalu associated with a natural or man-made crisis or disaster.

condition.narrative: The Recipient shall establish no later than four (4) months after the Effective Date, the Project Steering Committee (“PSC”), inform and resources satisfactory to the Association and which shall be chaired by the Minister of Health, or his or her delegate,and comprising of representatives from the Ministry of Finance, as provided under the Project Operations Manual [Section I.A.1].

The Recipient shall establish no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, a Project Management Unit (PMU), within theMoH, with a mandate, composition and resources satisfactory to the Association, which shall be responsible for, inter alia,carryingout day-to-day implementation of Parts 1, 2 and 3 of Project, with support from the CPMO. To this end, the Recipient shallno later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, recruit and thereafter maintain at all times during implementation of theProject, the following minimum staff and/or personnel: (i) a Project manager; (ii) a procurement officer; and (iii) a Projectaccountant; each with terms of reference, qualifications and experience satisfactory to the Association [Section I.A.3 and SectionI.A.4].

The Recipient shall prepare and furnish to the Association, by not later than September 30 of each year during the implementationof the Project (or such other interval or date as the Association may agree), for the Association's review and no-objection, anAnnual Work Plan and Budget, which shall, inter alia: (a) list all activities (including Operating Costs and Training) proposed tobe included in the Project in the Recipient's following fiscal year; (b) provide a budget for their financing (with a financialplan specifying all sources of financing including the Financing and any other resources provided by the Recipient); and (c)describe the environmental and social safeguards measures taken or planned to be taken in accordance with the provisions of SectionI.E of this Schedule 2 [Section I.C.1].

The Recipient shall, no later than four (4) months after the Effective Date (or such other date which the Association has confirmedin writing to the Recipient is reasonable and acceptable under the circumstances, as determined by the Association in its solediscretion), prepare and furnish to the Association for its review and no-objection a Project operations manual, afford theAssociation a reasonable opportunity to review the proposed Project Operations Manual; and adopt the Project Operations Manual asaccepted by the Association [Section I.B1].

title.narrative: Increase in the percentage of screened adults with a 10-year cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk =30% or with existing hypertension or diabetes that are being managed for their condition

comment.narrative: Proxy data available only: As of 2024 there were cumulatively 1998 persons screened for NCD. This is calculated as the "Number of Registrations." Of these registered people, 90% were visited at home, and 253 (14%) were referred for further management. Since there is no monitoring system in place it is not known how many of these 253 patients are currently being treated and how they are being treated.

title.narrative: Strategy determined for having functional and fit for purpose Hospital Management Information System

baseline.value: Current Hospital Management Information does not fully work across hospital departments, is designed for a large tertiary facility, includes text in foreign characters, and is not sufficiently maintained.

target.value: A strategy would be agreed for adapting or replacing HMIS with a costed and specific action plan

comment.narrative:
September update: Related project activities to assess the HMIS are at the early consultation stage.
Definition at appraisal: The strategy will include an assessment of the existing system and the health information echo-system; definition of the functionality (clinical, administrative, technical) required; definition of the context in terms of human resources, technical capabilities, etc.; analysis of options to replace or update of the HMIS based on cost and feasibility; and detailed plan based on the preferred option.

actual.value: Review of HMIS pending Digital Health Strategy reccomendations.

title.narrative: Increase in the availability of essential hospital services at Princess Magraret Hospital

target.value: Availability of services increased at PMH in at least four service areas

comment.narrative:
September update: ???????On track. A health needs analysis (i.e. 'service needs assessment') is underway. The functional design is likely a year 3 deliverable which aligns with intermediate indicator 1 and the target date of 31-Dec-2025. 
Definition at appraisal: A service delivery assessment would be conducted in Year 1 and from that assessment agreement would be reached on a specific enhanced service delivery capacity at PMH. It is expected that tracer services would be agreed in four categories: (i) diagnostic, including radiological and public health; (ii) general surgery; (iii) mental health; and (iii) integrated approach to NCD management. The PDO indictor will measure the process of developing the PMH and ultimately the final target would be that the defined tracer services are in place and functional.
